title: Data Consistency & Event-Driven Patterns: Outbox, Idempotent Consumers, Sagas & Reconciliation
concept: Keep data correct when one business action spans a database, a broker and other services: the dual-write problem, transactional outbox and publisher, inbox deduplication, ordering per key, safe replay, sagas with compensation, reconciliation, and schema evolution for events.
description: An expert course for engineers whose system no longer fits in one transaction. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - an enrollment committed in PostgreSQL whose "enrolled" event never reached the certificate service, a wallet consumer an AI wrote that added points twice on redelivery, progress events applied out of order, a replay that doubled every score, a payment that succeeded while the enrollment step failed - and fixes it with a pattern you can test: the dual-write problem, the DB Commit Succeeded, Publish Failed scenario, outbox in the same transaction, an outbox publisher that survives crashes, inbox deduplication, ordering by aggregate, safe replay, eventual consistency, sagas and compensation, reconciliation, CDC versus outbox, schema evolution and monitoring. 15 lessons with True/False quizzes on real logs and timelines, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests on in-memory stores with transactions.

learningOutcomes.text: Explain the dual-write problem and close it with a transactional outbox
Make consumers idempotent with an inbox so redelivered events change nothing
Publish at least once, keep order per aggregate key and replay without doubling effects
Design for eventual consistency and reconcile drift between sources and read models
Coordinate multi-step flows with sagas and compensation, and evolve event schemas safely
